tasks.short: Work out costs of materials, overhead and expenses from quotes and price lists, and check invoices against them.

steps.what: Collect quotes, price lists and contract rates from mail and SharePoint

loop.input: PDF or mail quotation, price list or agency rate card
loop.output: price lines: supplier, item or service, unit, price, valid from/to, surcharge rules
loop.check: Totals in the document recomputed from extracted lines; supplier matched to AFAS creditor by KvK/VAT/IBAN; unit and currency from fixed lists
loop.stop: Two attempts per document; on failed check the document goes to the bookkeeper's queue for manual entry
loop.why_not_simpler: Quotes arrive as free-form PDFs and mails with no fixed layout, so fixed templates miss too many.

steps.what: Key prices and rates into the Excel cost sheet
Calculate costs and allocate overhead to sites and cost centres
Check supplier and agency invoice prices against the agreed rates
Send the cost overview to controller and FP&A

tasks.design: Replace the Excel cost sheet with a small price-register app on the governed data platform, fed by a bounded extraction loop for PDF quotes and rate cards and approved by the bookkeeper. A scheduled Python job computes costs and overhead allocations per site from AFAS volumes and checks every incoming AFAS invoice line against the register, sending only deviations above tolerance to the bookkeeper; results feed a Power BI page for controller and FP&A.
tasks.previous_blocker: Prices live in mails, PDFs and personal Excel sheets with no structure, so there was nothing to check invoices against automatically.
tasks.enabler_now: Models read free-form quotes well enough for a checked extraction loop, and AI-assisted coding makes a small register app and checking job a matter of days.
tasks.still_hard: Keeping the register current when rates change by phone or mail, and agreeing allocation keys for shared overhead across the three sites.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding whether a price deviation is a supplier error, a valid surcharge or a change someone agreed without telling finance, and raising it with the buyer.

ambition.what: Price check on every supplier and agency invoice line instead of spot checks on large invoices.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper stops retyping prices and spends the time on deviations; they gain the right to hold an invoice that breaks agreed rates and to approve register changes.

reach.task: Build cost assumptions for the forecast
reach.learn: How price and volume drivers feed the forecast, so register data serves both.
Why keys are chosen per site and how they affect margin per customer.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level, so line prices are available for checking.
PDF invoices are scanned into e-invoices in AFAS with supplier found by KvK, VAT and IBAN.
Coding suggestions from history still need team review for accountability.
A bounded model loop can extract price lines from free-form quotes with arithmetic checks.

assumptions: Agency rate cards and main supplier price lists exist in writing.
AFAS invoice lines carry item or service codes that can map to register lines.
Volume data per site is available in AFAS or a warehouse system extract.
unknowns: How many suppliers have agreed price lists versus ad-hoc quotes.
Which allocation keys the controller uses today for overhead per site.
Whether a governed data platform is already in place next to Power BI.
research_questions: What share of invoice lines by value can be mapped to a register price?
How often do invoices deviate from agreed rates, and what is the euro value per year?
Does AFAS allow price tolerance checks on invoice lines without custom code?
How accurate is the extraction loop on a sample of 50 real quotes?

tasks.short: Match daily Rabobank statement lines to open invoices and ledger postings in AFAS and clear differences.

steps.what: Import Rabobank CAMT.053 statements into AFAS
Review AFAS automatic matches
Search invoices and mails to match unmatched lines by hand

loop.input: Unmatched bank line with free-text description, plus open items and remittance mails for that IBAN
loop.output: Proposed match to one or more open items, or a booking proposal (bank costs, refund, unknown) with a short reason
loop.check: Proposed items must sum to the bank amount within set tolerance and belong to the same debtor or creditor; otherwise no proposal
loop.stop: One pass per line; no valid proposal leaves the line in the manual queue
loop.why_not_simpler: After AFAS rules on reference, IBAN and amount, the rest has messy descriptions, partial or combined payments that fixed rules cannot read.

steps.what: Ask collections, suppliers or customers about unknown receipts and payments
Post differences, bank costs and close the reconciliation

tasks.design: Set up the AFAS automatic CAMT.053 import and tune its matching rules and tolerances so most lines clear without touch. A scheduled job on the remaining lines runs a bounded model loop that reads descriptions and remittance mails and proposes matches that must sum exactly; the bookkeeper approves in AFAS, and a daily Teams notification lists open lines older than three days to collections.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rules only cover clean references; free-text descriptions, combined payments and remittance advice in mailboxes needed a person to read them.
tasks.enabler_now: AFAS already offers rule-based bank matching with tolerances, and a model can read the leftover free text while the amount check keeps it safe.
tasks.still_hard: Customers who pay many invoices in one amount without reference, and agency payments split between normal account and g-rekening.
tasks.human_edge: Judging unknown receipts and deciding when to call a customer or supplier, and booking differences that affect the ledger.

ambition.what: Daily instead of weekly reconciliation, so DSO and cash position are current every morning.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper reviews a short exception list each morning instead of matching for hours; they own the matching rules and tolerances in AFAS.

reach.learn: How unapplied cash leads to wrong dunning letters and how faster matching avoids them.

reach.task: Month-end bank and suspense account review
reach.learn: What the accountant needs to sign off bank balances at close.

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums, with optional tolerance; misses go to a person.
AP and bank processes should run with people on exceptions and every decision logged with its data.
A model can propose matches for free-text bank descriptions when an exact-sum check gates them.

assumptions: Rabobank delivers CAMT.053 to AFAS daily.
Outgoing AFAS invoices carry a payment reference customers often use.
Remittance advice arrives in a shared finance mailbox.
unknowns: Current auto-match rate in AFAS and how many lines go manual per week.
Whether AFAS matching rules and tolerances are already tuned.
How agency g-rekening payments show on the statement.
research_questions: What share of bank lines does AFAS auto-match today, and after tuning rules?
Of the remaining lines, how many could the loop match with an exact-sum check in a one-month backtest?
Can the loop read the shared mailbox under AVG rules agreed with the privacy officer?

tasks.short: Build AP, AR, cash and P&L tables and reports from AFAS exports in Excel.

steps.what: Export ageing, cash and ledger data from AFAS
Build pivots and format tables in Excel
Tie report totals to the ledger
Write comments on large items and movements

loop.input: Period-on-period variance table with top movements and their underlying invoices
loop.output: Short draft comment per material movement
loop.check: Every number in the draft is matched against the table by code; comments citing numbers not in the table are rejected
loop.stop: One draft per report; a failed check drops that comment and flags it for manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Explaining why a movement happened needs reading invoice descriptions and supplier names; templates give only empty phrases.

steps.what: Mail reports to controller, finance director and site managers

tasks.design: Move the recurring AP, AR and cash tables into Power BI on the nightly AFAS extract, with subscriptions instead of mailed Excel files. A scheduled job ties report totals to the trial balance and blocks publication on a mismatch, and a bounded loop drafts comments on top movements for the bookkeeper to edit.
tasks.previous_blocker: Reports grew as personal Excel files with manual tweaks, and nobody had time to rebuild them in Power BI.
tasks.enabler_now: The nightly AFAS extract in Power BI already exists, AI-assisted building makes report pages quick, and models can draft checked variance comments.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing one definition per report with the controller and retiring the old Excel versions people trust.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which movements matter to the business and what is behind them, from talks with sites and suppliers.

ambition.what: Site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo get their own weekly AP and cost view for the first time.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper no longer builds tables; they check comments and answer questions on the numbers, and own the report definitions with the controller.

reach.learn: Which AP and AR figures feed forecast accuracy and how to flag them early.

reach.task: Maintain Power BI datasets on the AFAS extract
reach.learn: How the shared extract is modelled and refreshed.

evidence.claim: Power BI dashboards on a nightly AFAS extract already exist at Noordhaven.
Variance commentary drafted by a model with numeric checks is feasible; no product cited.

assumptions: The nightly AFAS extract includes open items and ledger detail.
Recipients have Power BI licences or can get them.
unknowns: Which reports are made, for whom, and how often.
Whether site managers may see supplier-level cost data.
Power BI licence situation for site managers.
research_questions: How many recurring Excel reports exist and how many hours per month go into each?
Do recipients accept a Power BI page in place of the Excel file?
How often do the drafted comments need more than light edits in a three-month trial?

tasks.short: Run and check the month-end trial balance in AFAS before handing it to the accountant and controller.

steps.what: Check all postings are in: bank, invoices, agency costs, memorials
Run trial balance report in AFAS
Check suspense, intercompany and balance accounts for odd balances

loop.input: Flagged account with its postings for the period
loop.output: Short explanation of the likely cause (missing accrual, wrong cost centre, intercompany mismatch) and a draft correction entry
loop.check: Draft entry must balance and touch only the flagged accounts; explanation must cite posting numbers that exist
loop.stop: One pass per flagged account; no valid output leaves it for manual review
loop.why_not_simpler: The deterministic checks find odd balances; finding the cause needs reading posting descriptions across many lines.

steps.what: Investigate and post correction entries
Hand trial balance to accountant and controller

tasks.design: A scheduled job on the AFAS extract runs a close checklist daily in the last week: postings complete, suspense and intercompany balances zero, balances within expected ranges, and sends a Teams status to the bookkeeper and controller. Flagged accounts get a bounded loop that explains the cause and drafts a balancing correction, which the bookkeeper posts or rejects in AFAS.
tasks.previous_blocker: AFAS produces the trial balance, but the checks around it lived in a personal Excel checklist and in people's heads.
tasks.enabler_now: AI-assisted coding turns the Excel checklist into scheduled checks quickly, and models can read posting descriptions to explain odd balances.
tasks.still_hard: Setting expected ranges per account without many false alarms, and accruals that depend on information outside AFAS.
tasks.human_edge: Deciding which corrections are right and taking responsibility for the books toward the accountant and auditor.

ambition.what: A daily soft trial balance in the closing week instead of one check at month end, cutting days to close.

tasks.altitude: The bookkeeper starts close with a clean list of exceptions rather than hunting; they gain the right to sign off completeness before the accountant takes over.

reach.learn: Which correction entries the accountant rejects most and why.
What evidence auditors want for balance accounts, to log it during close.

evidence.claim: Bank matching in AFAS is rules-based with misses going to a person, feeding close completeness.
Keep people on exceptions and log every decision with its data.
Trial balance runs as a standard AFAS report.

assumptions: Each site is a separate administration or cost centre in AFAS with intercompany accounts.
A close checklist exists in some form today.
unknowns: Current days to close and where the delays are.
Number of administrations in AFAS and how intercompany is booked.
Which audit adjustments came up last year.
research_questions: Which checks on the current checklist find real errors, and how often?
How many audit adjustments last year would daily checks have caught?
Can expected ranges per account be set from twelve months of history with few false alarms?

role.altitude: Bookkeepers move from keying, matching and building tables to handling exceptions and owning match rules, tolerances, the price register and supplier data. They gain the right to hold invoices that break agreed rates and to sign off close completeness.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: unapplied cash and dunning
Accountant: month-end close and correction review
FP&A Analyst: cost drivers for the forecast
Controller: allocation keys and audit evidence
skills_to_grow: Setting and tuning AFAS matching rules and tolerances
Reading and testing simple data checks and Power BI reports
Reviewing model proposals critically and logging decisions
Supplier master data quality (IBAN, KvK, g-rekening)
role.ambitious_version: Finance runs a daily soft close: bank reconciled each morning, every invoice line checked against agreed prices, and a clean trial balance status every day of the closing week, so the team closes in fewer days with figures site managers also see.
